objectives: Name the common pets and where they come from.
List what every pet needs each day.
Feed a pet the right food and the right amount.
Tell when a pet needs the veterinary doctor.
Use the new words for pets and their things.
Keep a pet safe and keep your own hands clean.

sections.body:
A **pet** is an animal that lives with people. People keep pets for company, for work, or just for fun.

In Vietnam you can see many kinds of pet. Dogs and cats live in homes. There are goldfish in bowls and tanks. You can meet hamsters, rabbits, budgies and turtles in pet shops. Some families even keep a small dog or cat at a café.

Where do pets come from? Most come from a breeder or a pet shop. A breeder raises animals carefully and keeps them healthy. A pet shop sells animals to people who will care for them.

Some animals wait in a shelter for a new home. A shelter looks after sick and lost animals until someone adopts them. Adopting means you take an animal to live with you and to look after.

A wild animal is not a pet, even if you want one. A squirrel in the park is free, and it should stay free. It knows where to hide, how to find food, and how to live with other squirrels.

Having a pet is a job. Someone in the family feeds it, cleans its home, and takes it to the doctor. That job lasts for years.
examples: A pet is an animal that lives with us and needs our care.
I want to adopt a cat from the shelter.
That squirrel in the park is a wild animal, not a pet.
sections.heading: What a pet is, and where pets come from

sections.body:
Animals cannot tell you what is wrong. They show you instead. When you know what a pet needs, you can read those signals.

**Food and water.** Every animal needs clean water at all times. A water bowl should be washed every day, because old water collects dirt and heat. Food should be the kind made for that animal. Dog food is not for cats, and cat food is not for dogs.

**A safe home.** A pet needs a warm, dry place to sleep. Dogs need a corner of the house that is theirs. A cat needs a quiet high spot. A fish needs clean water with plants in it.

**Exercise and play.** Dogs need to walk every day. Cats need to chase something. Goldfish need room to swim, not a small bowl for life.

**Health.** A young animal needs injections to protect it from disease. An old animal needs to see the veterinary doctor more often.

**Kindness and time.** A pet needs company and gentle hands. Many animals are lonely all day while the family is at work or school.

**A clean space.** Bedding should be washed. A fish tank should be cleaned. Even a small hamster cage needs fresh bedding.
examples: I wash the water bowl every morning.
We give the dog food made for dogs.
The cat likes a quiet place high up in the room.
sections.heading: What every pet needs every day

sections.body:
Caring for a pet is a set of small jobs. Doing them in the same order each day makes them easy to remember, and the animal feels safe.

Start with the fresh water. Check the bowl, wash it, and fill it again.

Then give the food. Use the food and the amount on the tin. Do not guess. Too much food makes a pet heavy, and that is not kind to its body.

Next, clean the home. Pick up what the pet has left, and wash the bowl or the bedding.

Then play. Ten minutes of real play is worth more than an hour of ignoring it.

Last, look at the animal. Check the eyes, the coat and the way it walks. If something looks wrong, write down what you saw and tell an adult.
examples: I fill the water bowl with fresh water first.
This food is for cats, so the dog cannot have it.
His coat looks dull, so I tell my mother.
sections.heading: How to take care of a pet every day
steps: Wash the water bowl and fill it with fresh water.
Give the right food in the right amount.
Clean the bed, the basket or the tank.
Play with the pet for a while.
Look at its eyes, coat and walk.
Tell an adult if something looks wrong.

sections.body:
These are the words you will hear in a pet shop or at the veterinary doctor.

A **pet shop** is a place where people buy or adopt animals and the things they need.

A **veterinary doctor**, called a vet for short, is a person who treats sick animals.

A **collar** is a band that goes around a dog's neck. It can carry a name tag and a small bell.

A **leash** is the long strap you hold when you walk a dog. It keeps the dog safe near traffic.

A **kennel** is a small house or basket where a pet sleeps.

**Grooming** means cleaning and brushing an animal's fur, nails and teeth. Long-haired animals need it often.

A **litter tray** is a box of sand where a cat does its business. A **hamster wheel** is a round wheel a hamster runs in to keep fit.

terms.example: We went to the pet shop to buy a food bowl.
terms.gloss: A place where people buy or adopt animals and the things they need to live well.

terms.example: The vet says the puppy needs two more injections.
terms.gloss: A person whose job is to treat sick animals and to help keep them healthy.

terms.example: The dog's collar has our phone number on it.
terms.gloss: A band around a dog's neck that can carry a name tag and a small bell.

terms.gloss: A strap you hold when you walk a dog, so the dog stays safe near traffic.

terms.example: We brush the cat every week. That is grooming.
terms.gloss: Cleaning and brushing an animal's fur, nails and teeth to keep it healthy.

sections.body:
Two pets can live in the same home and still need completely different things.

A **dog** needs to go out several times a day. Dogs like to be with people, and they get sad when they are alone for long hours. A dog needs to walk on a leash in busy streets.

A **cat** is more independent. It sleeps a lot, likes to climb, and cleans itself. Cats should stay indoors, because streets are full of cars and other cats.

A **fish** lives in water. Its tank needs clean water, plants for shelter, and no tall rocks that could trap it. A goldfish cannot live in a tiny bowl. Fish feel the water temperature, and the water has to stay steady.

A **hamster** or a **rabbit** needs a cage with bedding to dig in, a wheel or space to run, and food made for small animals. A hamster's teeth keep growing, so it needs hard things to chew.

A **bird** needs a cage with room to fly inside, a perch to stand on, and a partner bird if it is a parrot. Birds are very smart and they get bored easily.

When you choose a pet, choose with your family. Choose the animal that fits your home, your time and your money. A pet lives as long as you care for it.
examples: The dog needs to go out three times today.
We keep the cat indoors so it is safe.
The hamster needs something hard to chew.
sections.heading: Different pets, different needs

sections.body:
Most bites from animals happen because the animal was scared, tired, hurt, or was carrying its own food. You can stop almost all of them.

Wash your hands before and after touching an animal, and after cleaning its space. This matters most with puppies, kittens and hamsters, because they can carry germs without being sick.

Never pull food out of a pet's mouth. Never lift a dog by its legs. Never wake a sleeping animal suddenly.

Some things are dangerous for pets. Chocolate, coffee, grapes and onion can make a dog very ill. Human medicine can kill a cat. Keep them away.

Do not leave a cat or a dog alone in a hot car. The temperature inside rises very fast, even on a mild day.

And if you are bitten or scratched, tell an adult straight away and wash the place with clean water. Small cuts can get infected, and a doctor can help quickly.
examples: I wash my hands after touching the hamster.
We stay in the shade with the dog because the ground is hot.
sections.heading: Keeping a pet, and yourself, safe

item.summary: A pet is an animal that lives with you and depends on you every day. After reading this, you can tell what different pets need, feed and care for one properly, and know the safety rules that keep both you and the animal well.
item.title: Pets and How to Care for Them
